newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo steel makers call for anti-dumping measures.
newsitem.headline: Yugo steel makers call for anti-dumping measures.

text.p: East European steel product imports are a threat to Yugoslav steel producers and should be prevented or limited by anti-dumping measures, a member of the Association of Yugoslav Steel Producers said on Wednesday.
"The prices of imported steel are 40 percent lower than the prices of domestic steel," association offficial Savo Markovic told Reuters.
"We have appealed to the federal government to consider preventing or limiting imports of steel at dumping prices," he said.
The association asked the government to restrict imports of some finished steel products, revise set quotas and regulations on customs duties that favour imports, Markovic said.
"We need a restrictive import quota system," he said.
"Our prices are not much above the prices of East European countries," Markovic said, adding: "But East European countries sell their steel products at dumping prices."
Finished steel product imports rose 67 percent to 123,500 tonnes in January-July from the same period in 1995. Markovic said about 90 percent of imports came from East European countries.

The two Yugoslav steel plants, Smederevo and Niksic, and eight other steel processors tripled their production of finished goods in the first seven months of the year, turning out 334,128 tonnes compared with 114,166 tonnes in the same period in 1995.
Steel production in the first seven months reached 293,511 tonnes, more than triple the previous year's output of 81,069 tonnes.
"In the same period, the production of the main Yugoslav steel (users) dropped 3.3 percent over the same period last year," Markovic said adding "this shows that we do not need such high imports."
